title: U.S. House · California's 34th District
area: Parts of central and eastern Los Angeles, including Downtown LA, Boyle Heights, East LA, Highland Park, Koreatown, Chinatown, and Eagle Rock.

context.text: California uses a top-two nonpartisan primary. In the June 2, 2026 primary, incumbent Jimmy Gomez (D) placed first with 46.0% and Angela Gonzales-Torres (D) placed second with 30.7%, so both Democrats advance to the November general election; no Republican advanced.

summary.text: Jimmy Gomez is the Democratic incumbent U.S. Representative for California's 34th District in Los Angeles, serving on the Ways and Means Committee and the House Intelligence Committee. A former labor organization political director, he served in the California State Assembly from 2012 to 2017 before winning a 2017 special election to Congress. He is seeking re-election, and the House Ethics Committee announced an investigation of him in August 2026.

background.text: According to his official biography, attended Riverside Community College before earning a B.A. in political science from the University of California, Los Angeles, and an M.A. in public policy from Harvard University's John F. Kennedy School of Government.
Served as the political director for the United Nurses Associations of California before entering politics.
Served in the California State Assembly, representing the 51st District, from 2012 to 2017; his official biography says he chaired the Assembly Appropriations Committee.
Was elected to Congress in a June 2017 special election and has represented the 34th District since.

In the 119th Congress sits on the Ways and Means Committee (Tax and Work and Welfare subcommittees) and the Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence; serves as a Deputy Whip for Policy of the Democratic Caucus and Deputy Whip for the Congressional Progressive Caucus.
Is the founder and chair of the Congressional Dads Caucus and the Congressional Renters Caucus and a member of the Congressional Hispanic Caucus and the Congressional Asian Pacific American Caucus.

On August 17, 2026, the House Ethics Committee announced it is reviewing allegations that Gomez may have engaged in sexual misconduct, including inappropriate sexual contact with a House staffer; the committee said the existence of an inquiry does not itself indicate a violation occurred. Gomez said he has made 'personal mistakes' outside his marriage but that his actions were consensual and did not violate the law or House Ethics rules, and that he respects the Committee's process.
According to his official biography, lives in Eagle Rock with his wife and son.

priorities.text: In his most recent completed Ballotpedia survey (2020), described himself as a 'working-class progressive' and cited co-sponsoring the Green New Deal, Medicare for All, the Rent Relief Act, the George Floyd Justice in Policing Act, and the American Dream and Promise Act.
priorities.quote: I am a co-sponsor of the Green New Deal, Medicare for All, the Rent Relief Act, the George Floyd Justice in Policing Act, and the American Dream and Promise Act.

positions.summary: Cosponsored H.R. 3115, the Assault Weapons Ban of 2025, and H.R. 18, the Bipartisan Background Checks Act of 2025 (119th Congress).
Cosponsored H.R. 4099, the Ensuring Women’s Right to Reproductive Freedom Act, and H.R. 10600, the Abortion is Health Care Everywhere Act of 2026 (119th Congress).
Cosponsored H.R. 2743, the Raise the Wage Act of 2025 (119th Congress).
Cosponsored H.Con.Res. 40 (Iran) and H.Con.Res. 68 (Venezuela), each directing the removal of U.S. Armed Forces from hostilities (119th Congress).

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Ways and Means (Tax and Work and Welfare subcommittees) and the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence in the 119th Congress (2025–2026).

summary.text: Angela Gonzales-Torres is a Democrat and, by her own description, a democratic socialist running for California's 34th District. A Highland Park native, she has worked in higher-education counseling and affordable-housing programs and has held local civic roles including president of the Highland Park Neighborhood Council. She placed second in the June 2026 top-two primary and is running against fellow Democrat Jimmy Gomez on affordability, accountability, access and ending ICE and for-profit prisons.

background.text: According to her campaign website, was born and raised in Highland Park, the daughter of a deportee raised by a single mother who relied on programs such as SNAP and Medicaid.
Describes herself as a lifelong Angeleno and 'the daughter of a deportee' whose path went from community organizer to congressional candidate.
background.quote: Angela Gonzales-Torres is a lifelong Angeleno, the daughter of a deportee, and an equity and justice advocate.

background.text: According to her campaign website, she pursued higher education and now works supporting people transitioning from prison into universities, and promotes intergenerational permanent affordable housing. Ballotpedia describes her as an academic counselor at Pasadena City College and a program director for a permanent affordable housing project.
Has served as president of the Highland Park Neighborhood Council, as a regional representative on Metro's Public Safety Advisory Committee, and in the Los Angeles Mayor's Office.
Describes herself as a democratic socialist; Ballotpedia reports she has been endorsed by Leaders We Deserve, the Democratic Socialists of America's Los Angeles chapter, and Justice Democrats.
Placed second in the June 2, 2026 nonpartisan primary with 30.7% of the vote (36,708 votes), advancing to a same-party general election against incumbent Jimmy Gomez.

priorities.text: Campaign lists four priorities: 'Affordability' (fighting for working people), 'Accountability' (equitably taxing and investing), 'Access' (funding education and youth programs), and 'Abolition' (ending ICE and for-profit prisons).

positions.summary: Campaign site says she is co-sponsoring Medicare for All and investing in mental health, addiction care, and local clinics for everyone regardless of immigration status or income.
positions.quote: Angela is fighting to make that a reality by co-sponsoring Medicare for All, investing in mental health and addiction care, and strengthening local clinics that serve everyone, regardless of immigration status or income.

positions.summary: Campaign site says she is fighting for a 'community-driven Green New Deal' prioritizing renewable energy and unionized green jobs.
positions.quote: Angela is fighting for a bold, community-driven Green New Deal that prioritizes renewable energy, unionized green jobs, and neighborhood-level projects like rooftop gardens, urban farms, and native plant healing spaces.

positions.summary: Campaign site calls for expanding Housing Choice Vouchers and emergency rental assistance, a right to an attorney in eviction court, and prosecution of corporate landlords for tenant harassment.
positions.quote: A legally-enshrined right to housing, and a right to an attorney in eviction court

positions.summary: Her campaign homepage lists "Abolition: Ending ICE & for-profit prisons" among her four priorities.
Campaign site calls for a federal wealth tax on the ultra-rich and says she will support the Make Billionaires Pay Their Fair Share Act.
positions.quote: Support a federal wealth tax on the ultra-rich.

positions.summary: Campaign site calls for an immediate arms embargo on Israel and says she will never vote to send weapons to the Israeli military.
positions.quote: will never vote to send weapons to the Israeli military

researchNotes: Gomez has not completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey and no current issues page was found on his campaign materials, so his 2026 priorities/positions rely on his last completed (2020) survey, cited as dated context. Gonzales-Torres has not completed a Candidate Connection survey; her positions come from her campaign website. Federal key votes and FEC finance totals for both candidates are added separately by script. Biography gaps: Gomez's official bio does not give a birth year or birthplace; Gonzales-Torres's materials do not list degrees, institutions or employers by name beyond what is cited, and no birth year was found.
